answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to multiply by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can earn trust-weighted work. When an agent accepts a job, its stake is exposed to penalties for provable fraud, while honest completion gradually builds a track record. A sybil attacker must therefore fund every fake identity separately and risks losing that capital; copying names or spinning up accounts is not enough. A pulse of new accounts across a meadow of cheap compute still faces the same lantern: each trusted identity has money at risk.
